model: The Dancing Demon — Plate–Continent Relationship Framework
active_rule: Many-to-many spatial intersection; no mandatory one-continent-one-plate containment
principles: Continents are geographic landmasses; tectonic plates are lithospheric regions.
Continental coastlines do not need to coincide with plate boundaries.
A continent may span multiple plates.
A plate may contain continental and oceanic crust.
Plate-face labels are provisional identifiers and do not establish crust type or exclusive continent assignment.

prior_test.question: Can all six continents fit entirely inside their same-named carrier plates under one common globe rotation?
prior_test.outcome: No common orientation found in 40000 deterministic random rotations plus coarse grid
prior_test.interpretation: Rejects the strict one-to-one containment requirement only; does not invalidate the plate partition or prove that a valid geographic overlay is impossible.

not_yet_validated: relief, bathymetry, climate, circulation, hydrology and biomes
